card.title: Nintendo Switch Motherboard Short Circuit and M92T36 Diagnostic Procedure

claims.statement: The USB charger fuse can be tested for continuity with a multimeter to verify power path to the battery chip.
claims.evidence: Continuity across both sides of the fuse indicates a good fuse; lack of continuity means it must be replaced.
claims.quote: Lets check the fuse that lets power from USB C reach the battery chip. Unplug the battery. With a multimeter set to continuity mode, put one probe in one side of the fuse and the other probe in the other side of the fuse

claims.statement: BQ24193 charge controller operation can be verified by checking battery voltage rise after 30 minutes of charging.
claims.evidence: If battery voltage increases after 30 minutes on the charger, the BQ24193 is functioning.
claims.quote: If the voltage after 30 minutes is higher than it was, you can assume that your console is charging so the BQ24193 is fine.

claims.statement: Capacitors shorted to ground on both sides indicate a shorted rail or bad component.
claims.evidence: Checking capacitors with a multimeter in continuity mode against ground shows continuity on only one side normally; continuity on both sides indicates a short.
claims.quote: It's supposed to have continuity in one of the sides of the capacitor, continuity in both sides of the capacitor means short to ground.

claims.statement: Pin 5 and Pin 6 of the M92T36 chip can be tested for input and output voltages using DC voltage mode.
claims.evidence: Pin 5 and Pin 6 should read between 3v to 6v; 0v on pin 6 indicates a bad M92T36 chip.
claims.quote: Put the main board back in the switch frame... touch the pin 5 of M92T36... In that pin you are supposed to have 3v to 6v... 0v in pin 6 means M92T36 is bad.

claims.statement: A faulty PI3USB30532 or dead CPU can cause the console to fail payload injection into RCM mode if the firmware/screen is otherwise okay.
claims.evidence: If Hekate payload fails via RCM, the PI3USB30532 may be bad or the CPU is dead.
claims.quote: If even the payload method failed, you probably will have a PI3USB30532 bad or the CPU is just dead af.

procedure: Unplug the battery and check the USB-C fuse for continuity using a multimeter.
Test BQ24193 voltages or monitor battery voltage increase after 30 minutes of charging.
Check capacitors and M92T36 pins for shorts to ground using a multimeter in continuity mode with the black probe on a good ground.
Test M92T36 pin 5 and pin 6 input/output voltages using a multimeter set to DC voltage.
Visually inspect the screen and backlight ribbon cables and connectors.
Attempt to boot into RCM mode and inject the latest Hekate payload if the screen remains black.
tools: Fine-tip multimeter probe or soldered paper pin
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Using third-party docks or non-standard USB-C cables can damage the charging port or brick the console.
card.caveats: If capacitors behind the CPU show a short to ground, the board is likely unrepairable.
